thesis: Cross-asset signals turned to relief (dollar index below 100, VIX 15.99, oil -5%, junk bonds up), but the 10-year yield sits at a 4.745% multi-year high, three Fed members voted to hike, only 5 of 12 sectors rose last week, and Friday's jobs report lands inside the holding window. The book owns what the market just showed it will pay for, AI revenue that is actually being billed (GOOGL, MSFT, AMZN), balanced by two low-beta names with fresh good news that react to rates in opposite ways: JPM gains if yields rise and BMY holds up if growth wobbles. It avoids every company reporting this week (AMD, CAT, LLY/AMGN/REGN, DIS, EQIX/WELL, the energy names) and the dividend stocks hurt by rising rates, utilities and REITs. Cash is 30%, near the Council's 35% target for jobs week and its rule to cut size by a quarter when VIX is under 16, trimmed slightly because the risk signals turned green and, against SPY, cash is itself a bet on the market falling.
risks: A strong jobs or wage number could push the 10-year through 4.75% toward 5% and hit GOOGL, MSFT and AMZN together (38% of the book riding one AI/cloud theme), and last week's 3.8% yen jump leaves a risk that borrowed-yen trades unwind and markets sell off. If instead chip stocks squeeze higher after AMD reports or the rally broadens, the 30% cash and the missing NVDA/AAPL weight will lag SPY; I have no memory of how this week actually went and used none.
